title: Hadji-Khan Dzhandarov
notes: This historical photograph, cataloged as number 3504, was taken by the photographer Dmitry Ivanovich Ermakov between the 1870s and 1890s. The image captures Hadji-Khan Dzhandarov and a female companion, in Loovsky aul, an Abaza settlement located in the Kuban Oblast of the Russian Empire, which is known today as the village of Krasny Vostok in the Karachay-Cherkess Republic. Original prints and negatives from this ethnographic series are preserved today within the permanent collections of the ROSPHOTO State Museum and Exhibition Centre in Saint Petersburg. and some sources inform that this edition was a part of J. Guthrie Watson's album. J. Guthrie Watson (c. 1850–1913) was an English traveller. A member of the Conservative Club in London, Watson appears to have been a former military officer and was, in his words, “well acquainted with the Caucasus (particularly that portion known as Circassia).” In 1889 he embarked on a journey across the Russian Empire, which included Circassia in the North Caucasus. He published the photo-album “A Journey Across Russia” upon his return to England in 1889. It is not certain how many of the views in this album were photographed by Watson himself. In 1899 he exhibited a collection of photographs at the Anthropological Institute in London.

title: Klishbi Aisovich Adzhigiriev
notes: Klishbi Aisovich Adzhigiriev (born 1876), a Kabardian man from the village of Nartan in the Chegemsky district, Kabardino-Balkaria. For the Soviet authorities, the social background of the Adzhigiriev family served as an indicator of "anti-Soviet sentiment." In December 1931, at the age of 55, Klishbi was arrested and accused of "preparing an armed uprising against Soviet power." In 1989, Klishbi Adzhigiriev was fully rehabilitated. Klishbi had six children; his wife was from the Ashabokov family. Two of his sons were executed by firing squad in 1937. Another son, Mukhametgeri, returned to the Kabardino-Balkarian ASSR after his period of exile.
